Get started with FunMel

Mitra Ghotbi

Source: vignettes/FunMel.Rmd
FunMel.Rmd

From a plate photograph to a matched response

This guide introduces the FunMel workflow: analyze plate photographs, inspect segmentation masks, organize experimental metadata, calculate matched-control melanization coefficients, assess treatment effects and export comparison figures. FunMel retains the original MycoHalo functions for compatibility.

The first worked example uses a bundled measured dataset from a 14-day confrontation assay. Subsequent examples use simulated plates and measurements to demonstrate image analysis and statistical methods. All runnable examples in this guide use bundled or simulated inputs; no photograph download is needed.

The default assay has four approximately round Zymoseptoria tritici colonies surrounding a central fungal colony and its halo candidate. Target-colony MI quantifies darkness in the four Z. tritici colonies. The central fungus and halo are measured separately and excluded from those MI summaries. A known inoculation layout supplies search regions and seeds. Detected outlines need not be round. These are image classes, not automated species identification. A central colour zone is a halo candidate, not a confirmed inhibition boundary.

The assay at a glance
Four target Zymoseptoria tritici colonies surround a central fungal colony. FunMel measures target-colony darkness and geometry, separates the central partner and halo candidate, and compares each treatment with its own controls.

Follow the workflow

Step Action Result
1 · Analyze Set the plate layout and dish diameter Target-colony measurements
2 · Review Inspect masks, calibration and warnings Documented quality decisions
3 · Match Identify independent plates and their control sets Verified experimental metadata
4 · Compare Calculate matched coefficients and assess a supported model Descriptive responses and, when justified, inference
5 · Communicate Export plate-level figures and tables Traceable results for reporting

Three essentials before starting: MI is an image-darkness proxy, not melanin concentration. Colonies within a dish are subsamples, not independent plates. Each treatment uses only the controls assigned to its matching set.

Install FunMel

Install a GitHub-hosted copy of the package using remotes. R >= 4.1 and source-compilation tools are required: Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, the matching Rtools release on Windows, or an R development toolchain and ImageMagick development libraries on Linux.

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel")
library(FunMel)

The source repository is mghotbi/FunMel. The default installation uses its default branch. To select a release tag or another branch, add ref="TAG_OR_BRANCH".

To include the locally installed vignette:

install.packages(c("remotes", "knitr", "rmarkdown"))
remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel",
                        build_vignettes=TRUE, dependencies=TRUE)
vignette("FunMel", package="FunMel")

Vignette building requires Pandoc, normally supplied with RStudio. Private repositories require GitHub authentication. Restart R before replacing a loaded FunMel installation. For a downloaded source archive, use install.packages(file.choose(), repos=NULL, type="source") instead.

Explore the measured 14-day case study

The bundled 14-day dataset contains twenty photographs organized into five matching sets. Each set contains one control dish and three treatment dishes, with four target Z. tritici colonies per dish. Metadata has twenty plate rows; the measurement table has eighty colony rows. This design is used to demonstrate shared-control matching. Other experiments may have different replicate counts and control arrangements, which must be recorded explicitly in their metadata.

real_meta <- read.csv(system.file("extdata","14_day_example","metadata.csv",
                                 package="FunMel"),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
real_colonies <- read.csv(system.file("extdata","14_day_example","colonies.csv",
                                     package="FunMel"),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
validate_metadata(real_meta)
knitr::kable(real_meta[real_meta$set_id=="A33_1_14_days",
                       c("file","plate_id","set_id","treatment","replicate")])
file plate_id set_id treatment replicate
2026_10_02_99_28.JPG 2026_10_02_99_28 A33_1_14_days control 1
2026_10_02_99_29.JPG 2026_10_02_99_29 A33_1_14_days A33_1 1
2026_10_02_99_31.JPG 2026_10_02_99_31 A33_1_14_days A33_1 2
2026_10_02_99_32.JPG 2026_10_02_99_32 A33_1_14_days A33_1 3

The same four-row structure applies to A60, B20, B22 and B37, with each set’s own control. The control replicate is 1 and the three treatment replicates are 1–3. Replicate numbers do not define one-to-one pairing here: all three treatment plates use their set’s single control. Folder-derived treatment identities and experimental mappings are provisional. Each control dish appears once in the metadata and serves as the denominator for all treatment plates in its set.

These are measured image-darkness values rather than simulated outputs. Interpretation as biological treatment responses requires verification of experimental assignments, segmentation masks and colour calibration. The bundled example retains its provisional review status.

plot_treatment_comparison(real_colonies,preview=TRUE)

For each set, the displayed coefficient is mean(MI_T1, MI_T2, MI_T3) / MI_control. This descriptive coefficient permits one control plate. The built-in inferential assessment has a separate replication guard and does not treat four control colonies as four control plates. Replicate ratios share control uncertainty; their spread is not a full ratio confidence interval. metadata_confirmed=FALSE is retained, so the figure is clearly provisional and final coefficient calculation remains blocked until review.

source(system.file("examples","04_14_day_case_study.R",package="FunMel"))
file.copy(system.file("examples","metadata_14_day_case_study.csv",package="FunMel"),
          "case_study_metadata.csv",overwrite=FALSE)

The case-study metadata illustrates one row per independent plate and explicit matching-set assignments. The following sections use synthetic data to explain image analysis and statistical calculations step by step.

1. Analyze and review a plate 

lay <- plate_layout(centre="none")
sim <- simulate_plate(width=400,height=500,layout=lay,seed=21)
control <- analyze_plate(sim$image,layout=lay,id="synthetic_control",
                         n_boot=20,verbose=FALSE)
control$colonies[,c("colony_id","detected","MI_mean","area_mm2")]
#>    colony_id detected  MI_mean area_mm2
#> x         TL     TRUE 46.76874 155.3031
#> x1        TR     TRUE 52.94210 154.8631
#> x2        BR     TRUE 57.78119 154.8631
#> x3        BL     TRUE 42.08680 155.5230
plot_qc(control)

There is one measurement row per target colony. The overlay shows boundaries and labels; the resolved-object panel shows the assigned regions. Four detected regions are not proof of four correct biological objects. Check dish scale, colony boundaries, reflections, central-object assignment and warnings.

fungal_layout <- plate_layout(centre="fungus",rotation_deg=10)
fungal_sim <- simulate_plate(width=400,height=500,layout=fungal_layout,seed=22)
confrontation <- analyze_plate(fungal_sim$image,layout=fungal_layout,
                               id="synthetic_fungal",n_boot=20,verbose=FALSE)
confrontation$plate_summary[,c("central_partner_type","central_detected","halo_status")]
#>   central_partner_type central_detected        halo_status
#> x               fungus             TRUE candidate_detected
plot_qc(confrontation)

For fungal confrontation photographs, use centre="fungus"; control plates use centre="none". Pass an image path rather than sim$image and enter the actual dish diameter:

img <- file.choose()
r <- analyze_plate(img,layout=plate_layout(centre="fungus"),
                   dish_diameter_mm=90,keep_images=TRUE)
plot_qc(r)
r$warnings

keep_images=TRUE allows later QC plotting. Batch results save QC PNGs but drop large image arrays. Mean MI is 100 - L* on retained, non-specular colony-interior pixels: higher MI means darker images, not measured pigment concentration.

2. Set the inoculation layout 

plate_layout(centre="fungus",rotation_deg=15,radius_frac=0.5)
#> <funmel_layout> 4 fungal colonies; centre: fungus
#>  id  x_rel  y_rel
#>  TL -0.250 -0.433
#>  TR  0.433 -0.250
#>  BR  0.250  0.433
#>  BL -0.433  0.250
positions <- data.frame(id=c("N","E","S","W"),
                        x_rel=c(0,0.5,0,-0.5),y_rel=c(-0.5,0,0.5,0))
plate_layout(centre="fungus",positions=positions)
#> <funmel_layout> 4 fungal colonies; centre: fungus
#>  id x_rel y_rel
#>   N   0.0  -0.5
#>   E   0.5   0.0
#>   S   0.0   0.5
#>   W  -0.5   0.0

Coordinates are relative to the dish radius: x increases rightward and y downward. radius_mm can set physical inoculation spacing. search_frac controls core-search radius. Do not enlarge it indiscriminately to capture unrelated growth. Optional numeric rotation_deg, radius_frac, radius_mm, search_frac, start_deg and n_colonies metadata columns are read by layout_by_treatment(). Explicit layout arguments take priority. Arbitrary image names and supported layouts are allowed; severely merged colonies, reflections or uncertain class identity still need review/training or manual analysis.

3. Match treatments to their controls

One row is one independently prepared dish photographed once. Four colonies on one plate are subsamples. Multiple photographs of the same dish are repeated observations, not independent biological replicates.

Field Required interpretation
file, relative_file Unique basename and optional path from the photo root
plate_id Unique biological plate ID
set_id Matching control set, often a batch
treatment control or a consistent intervention name
centre_model none for controls; fungus for fungal confrontation
partner_type Biological partner type
zymo_strain, day, medium Recommended context, complete and constant within a set if supplied
metadata_confirmed TRUE after experimental mapping is verified
qc_pass TRUE after acceptable mask and calibration review; required for finalization

A treatment in S1 uses only S1 controls. Separate treatment-control experiments need separate set IDs. Several treatments can legitimately share controls within one batch: put all those plates in one set and list each control once. Do not copy a shared control under new plate IDs. The same treatment label across sets must mean the same intervention. Set IDs need not be folder names.

demo <- example_experiment(seed=42)
# Assign fungal labels to the two simulated treatment groups.
fungal_labels <- stats::setNames(c("fungus_A", "fungus_B"),
  setdiff(unique(as.character(demo$metadata$treatment)), "control"))
for (component in c("metadata", "colonies")) {
  d <- demo[[component]]
  d$treatment <- ifelse(d$treatment == "control", "control",
    fungal_labels[as.character(d$treatment)])
  for (field in intersect(c("centre_model", "partner_type"), names(d)))
    d[[field]] <- ifelse(d$treatment == "control", "none", "fungus")
  demo[[component]] <- d
}
validate_metadata(demo$metadata)
with(demo$metadata,table(set_id,treatment))
#>       treatment
#> set_id control fungus_A fungus_B
#>     S1       3        3        3
#>     S2       3        3        3
#>     S3       3        3        3
knitr::kable(head(demo$metadata[,c("file","plate_id","set_id","treatment","centre_model")]))
file plate_id set_id treatment centre_model
P001.jpg P001 S1 control none
P002.jpg P002 S1 control none
P003.jpg P003 S1 control none
P004.jpg P004 S1 fungus_A fungus
P005.jpg P005 S1 fungus_A fungus
P006.jpg P006 S1 fungus_A fungus

This synthetic design has three shared-control batches, each with control, fungus_A and fungus_B and three independent plates per group. Its true MI increments are 8 and 15, with added plate and colony variation. Plate IDs are unambiguous; treatment C must not reuse an ID like C1 that also names a control.

make_metadata("photos",recursive=TRUE)
# Edit photos/plate_metadata.csv: fill experimental fields, do not guess them.
meta <- read.csv("photos/plate_metadata.csv",stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
files <- file.path("photos",meta$relative_file)
validate_metadata(meta,files)
# Alternative for any original photo ZIP, including enclosing folders:
files <- prepare_photo_archive("original_photos.zip",meta,"extracted_photos")

Review metadata before finalization

  1. Create or load metadata. New templates include metadata_confirmed and qc_pass, both initially FALSE. For an older table without the QC column:

    if (!"qc_pass" %in% names(metadata)) metadata$qc_pass <- FALSE

  2. Review every independent plate. Inspect the target-colony masks, central fungus/halo candidate, calibration and warnings. Verify treatment labels and the set_id that links each treatment to its own controls. Mark only reviewed plates as passing; replace the example IDs below:

    reviewed_ids <- c("plate_1", "plate_2")
metadata$qc_pass[metadata$plate_id %in% reviewed_ids] <- TRUE
# Separately confirm experimentally verified metadata rows:
confirmed_ids <- c("plate_1", "plate_2")
metadata$metadata_confirmed[metadata$plate_id %in% confirmed_ids] <- TRUE

  3. Save and finalize when every included plate is ready. The metadata must contain exactly the analyzed plate IDs. Both flags must be logical TRUE for every included plate, with no missing values. Use TRUE and FALSE without quotation marks. Resolve failed images and unacceptable QC before finalization; the flags record user review, not automatic approval.

    write.csv(metadata, "plate_metadata_reviewed.csv", row.names = FALSE)
reviewed <- finalize_analysis(result, metadata)

Here metadata is the reviewed metadata data frame and result is the batch result returned by analyze_plates(); use the actual object names in the analysis. Adding a review column does not require repeating image processing. Changing segmentation settings or a central-partner recipe does require reanalysis.

The template includes logical metadata_confirmed and qc_pass columns, both initially FALSE. Review each plate’s masks and calibration, and verify its treatment and matching control set before changing its flags to TRUE. For an existing CSV without qc_pass, add metadata$qc_pass <- FALSE in R or add a qc_pass column in the CSV. Finalization requires both flags to be TRUE for every included plate; adding a review column does not require repeating image analysis.

The template records provenance but leaves unknown experimental fields blank and metadata_confirmed=FALSE. Validation checks unique files/plates, complete set IDs, controls within each set and constant recorded matching contexts. Different strains, days or media should have separate set IDs. Final pooling of multiple recorded contexts requires an explicit pool_contexts=TRUE decision. It is not a default biological recommendation.

The twenty-row case-study metadata is available as inst/examples/metadata_14_day_case_study.csv, introduced at the start of this guide. Use it as a worked example; create a separate metadata table for each new experiment rather than reusing its assignments.

4. Calculate the melanization coefficient

Average target-colony MI within each plate, giving each colony equal weight. Then average independent plate means within set and treatment, giving each plate equal weight. The ratio is

MIp=1np∑jMIpj,MCs,t=mean⁡p∈(s,t)MIpmean⁡p∈(s,control)MIp. MI_p=\frac{1}{n_p}\sum_j MI_{pj},\qquad MC_{s,t}=\frac{\operatorname{mean}_{p\in(s,t)} MI_p} {\operatorname{mean}_{p\in(s,control)} MI_p}. 

d <- data.frame(plate_id=rep(c("C01","T01","T02","T03"),each=4),
                set_id="S1",treatment=rep(c("control","A","A","A"),each=4),
                colony_id=rep(c("TL","TR","BR","BL"),4),
                MI_mean=rep(c(40,48,52,56),each=4))
mc <- melanization_coefficient(d)
mc$plate_means
#>   plate_id treatment set_id MI_plate n_target_colonies n_colonies_used
#> 1      C01   control     S1       40                 4               4
#> 2      T01         A     S1       48                 4               4
#> 3      T02         A     S1       52                 4               4
#> 4      T03         A     S1       56                 4               4
#>   n_colonies_excluded
#> 1                   0
#> 2                   0
#> 3                   0
#> 4                   0
mc$per_plate_coefficients[,c("plate_id","melanization_coefficient")]
#>   plate_id melanization_coefficient
#> 1      T01                      1.2
#> 2      T02                      1.3
#> 3      T03                      1.4
mc$coefficients[,c("MI_treatment_mean","MI_control_mean","melanization_coefficient")]
#>   MI_treatment_mean MI_control_mean melanization_coefficient
#> 1                52              40                      1.3

The replicate ratios are 1.2, 1.3 and 1.4; the treatment coefficient is mean(48,52,56)/40 = 1.3. Independent plate measurements remain available for analysis. This is not a mean of position-specific ratios. The partner is excluded using target flags/central IDs. Missing target MI is an error by default; na_action="omit" is an explicit documented-exclusion option. A whole unusable plate remains unavailable. A nonpositive control denominator gives no ratio.

If a treatment occurs in several sets, its overall descriptive coefficient is an equal-set mean of matched ratios, not a ratio against pooled unrelated controls.

x <- data.frame(plate_id=c("C1","T1","C2","T2"),set_id=c("S1","S1","S2","S2"),
                treatment=c("control","A","control","A"),colony_id="TL",
                MI_mean=c(20,40,80,80))
z <- melanization_coefficient(x)$coefficients
z[,c("set_id","melanization_coefficient")]
#>   set_id melanization_coefficient
#> 1     S1                        2
#> 2     S2                        1
mean(z$melanization_coefficient) # 1.5; pooled 120/100 would be 1.2
#> [1] 1.5

A ratio of 1.3 is not evidence of 30% more melanin. MI is an image-darkness proxy. Replicate-ratio SD/SE does not include uncertainty in a shared control denominator.

5. Assess treatment effects 

a <- assess_experiment(demo$colonies,comparison_scope="common_sets")
a$status
#> [1] "ok"
knitr::kable(a$overall_coefficients,digits=3)
treatment n_sets mean_matched_coefficient sd_across_sets sets
fungus_A 3 1.124 0.027 S1;S2;S3
fungus_B 3 1.278 0.073 S1;S2;S3 
# Preserve small p-values in the displayed tables; do not round them to zero.
format_tests <- function(x) {
  for(nm in intersect(c("p_value","p_adjusted"),names(x)))
    x[[nm]] <- base::format.pval(x[[nm]],digits=2,eps=0.001)
  x
}
knitr::kable(format_tests(a$overall_effects),digits=3)
treatment n_sets sets estimate se df lower upper p_value p_adjusted
fungus_A 3 S1;S2;S3 5.819 1.353 18 2.977 8.661 <0.001 <0.001
fungus_B 3 S1;S2;S3 12.950 1.353 18 10.108 15.792 <0.001 <0.001 
knitr::kable(format_tests(a$treatment_comparisons),digits=3)
treatment_1 treatment_2 n_common_sets sets_1 sets_2 comparison_scope same_set_coverage status estimate se df lower upper p_value p_adjusted
fungus_A fungus_B 3 S1;S2;S3 S1;S2;S3 common_sets TRUE ok -7.131 1.353 18 -9.973 -4.289 <0.001 <0.001

The descriptive ratios and inferential effects are different outputs. The mixed model uses original colony MI with one random intercept per independent plate:

MIspj=μs,t(p)+bp+ϵspj,bp∼N(0,σplate2),ϵspj∼N(0,σ2). MI_{spj}=\mu_{s,t(p)}+b_p+\epsilon_{spj},\quad b_p\sim N(0,\sigma^2_{plate}),\quad \epsilon_{spj}\sim N(0,\sigma^2).

Every observed set-treatment cell has its own fixed mean. lme4 fits this model; lmerTest gives Satterthwaite contrast inference. Within-set effects subtract that set’s control. A-versus-B compares matched effects, preserving shared-control covariance. No test treats treatment averages as biological replicates. An explicit method="plate_means" fits the same cell-specific fixed means to one arithmetic mean per plate; with unequal colony counts it need not match the mixed model’s weighting exactly.

comparison_scope="common_sets" uses shared sets only; an absent common set gives no_common_sets. The default matched_effects uses each treatment’s observed sets and flags different coverage. A treatment observed only in one batch cannot automatically be separated from batch-specific effects. Holm-adjusted p values are reported separately from unadjusted contrast-wise confidence intervals.

How this relates to the usual treatment-plus-batch model

The confrontation-assay principle is retained: independent replicate measurements, own-batch control normalization for interpretation, and modelling that accounts for experimental structure. FunMel’s cell-specific model estimates effects in observed sets; it does not fit a common treatment effect across random batches. An additive model instead assumes treatment differences are common across batches. For a sufficiently crossed design, the following is an advanced alternative on individual plate means, not treatment averages:

pm <- melanization_coefficient(demo$colonies)$plate_means
additive <- lm(MI_plate ~ treatment + factor(set_id),data=pm)
coef(additive)
#>       (Intercept) treatmentfungus_A treatmentfungus_B  factor(set_id)S2 
#>         41.756742          5.819055         12.949846          5.962451 
#>  factor(set_id)S3 
#>          9.513623

This example is separate from assess_experiment(), not an automatic fallback. Check estimability, residual variance and whether a common treatment effect is scientifically justified. A random-batch model such as lme4::lmer(MI_plate ~ treatment + (1 | set_id), data=pm) additionally requires an appropriate population-of-batches interpretation and enough batches to estimate variance. Very few batches can make this unstable. More complex factorial, longitudinal, spatial or heteroscedastic designs need their own models.

Replication and diagnostics

The built-in assessment requires at least two independent plates per cell and within-plate replication for its mixed model. This is a conservative computational guard, not a universal requirement of all confrontation assays or proof of power. One control plate still permits a descriptive ratio. Some sparse designs may support other justified models; additional assumptions must not be hidden.

sparse <- suppressWarnings(assess_experiment(d))
sparse$status # insufficient_plate_replication
#> [1] "insufficient_plate_replication"

Singular fits, convergence problems and insufficient replication return explicit status and withhold inferential tables. No significance test is silently substituted.

a$diagnostics$plates_per_cell
#>    set_id treatment  cell n_plates
#> 1      S1   control C0001        3
#> 4      S1  fungus_A C0002        3
#> 7      S1  fungus_B C0003        3
#> 10     S2   control C0004        3
#> 13     S2  fungus_A C0005        3
#> 16     S2  fungus_B C0006        3
#> 19     S3   control C0007        3
#> 22     S3  fungus_A C0008        3
#> 25     S3  fungus_B C0009        3
a$diagnostics$variance_components
#>        grp        var1 var2     vcov    sdcor
#> 1   .plate (Intercept) <NA> 7.945878 2.818843
#> 2 Residual        <NA> <NA> 1.160049 1.077056
op <- par(mfrow=c(1,2))
plot(fitted(a$model),residuals(a$model),xlab="Fitted MI",ylab="Residual")
abline(h=0,lty=2)
qqnorm(residuals(a$model));qqline(residuals(a$model))

par(op)

Spatial block-bootstrap intervals describe within-image pixel sampling, not plate-to-plate biological variation. Normality and equal residual variance remain model assumptions. Account for review/exclusion decisions and design limitations.

6. Process and finalize an experiment 

out <- analyze_plates(files,metadata=meta,
                      layout=function(row) layout_by_treatment(row),
                      qc_dir="FunMel_results/qc")
saveRDS(out,"FunMel_results/image_analysis.rds")
out$failed
out$coefficient_error
# STOP and inspect every QC image, measurement warning and metadata mapping.
# Correct images/masks if needed. Then edit the CSV's confirmation/review flags.
reviewed_meta <- read.csv("photos/plate_metadata.csv",stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
reviewed <- finalize_analysis(out,reviewed_meta)
write.csv(reviewed$melanization_coefficient,
          "FunMel_results/matched_coefficients.csv",row.names=FALSE)
saveRDS(reviewed,"FunMel_results/reviewed_analysis.rds")

finalize_analysis() requires explicit complete logical metadata_confirmed=TRUE and qc_pass=TRUE. These record user decisions, not automatic biological proof. It applies verified labels to saved measurements without repeating image processing. A changed central-partner recipe or layout requires reanalysis. Failed images must be resolved before finalization. Do not silently discard an inconvenient replicate. The generic scripts/analyse_experiment.R saves measurement tables, statuses and session information and separates the review stage from final assessment.

7. Export figures and statistics 

plot_treatment_comparison(demo,
  labels=c(fungus_A="Fungal partner A",fungus_B="Fungal partner B"))

p <- plot_treatment_comparison(reviewed,file="FunMel_results/treatment_comparison")
# Vector PDF/SVG, 600-dpi PNG and _statistics.csv are written.
attr(p,"FunMel_statistics") # means, SDs, independent plate counts, descriptive delta_MI

Panel A displays independent plate MI means and matching controls. Panel B displays treatment replicate ratios and the set’s ratio of means. Outlined squares are controls; coloured circles are treatment plates. Lower diamonds show treatment means, with bars spanning mean ± one between-plate SD. Each row reports control and treatment mean MI, treatment SD, coefficient and coefficient SD. A single control plate has no estimable SD (shown as unavailable). Shared controls remain shared, not new replicates. Coefficient SD measures treatment variability conditional on the shared control mean; it excludes denominator uncertainty. These SDs are not confidence intervals. The separate model results from assess_experiment() are needed for supported inferential comparisons. Inferential estimates and confidence intervals are reported separately by assess_experiment() when the design and model diagnostics support them. preview=TRUE labels a provisional view; it never confirms metadata or overrides failed QC. Figures need verified identities, adequate imaging and a suitable caption before publication. Export settings do not establish scientific validity.

8. Interpret outputs and resolve warnings

Output What it measures
MI_mean, MI_median Target-colony image darkness
area_mm2, circularity, solidity Detected mask geometry, conditional on scale and segmentation
delta_MI_facing Facing-minus-away darkness difference within a target
radial_asymmetry_pct Toward/away radial asymmetry; alias of legacy growth_inhibition_pct
gap_partner_mm Geometric gap to the detected central partner
profiles Distance-from-edge ring summaries, not independent plates
halo_status Resolved colour-zone candidate or unresolved boundary

Control-referenced growth inhibition is (C - T)/C * 100, with a specified, consistent growth outcome (e.g. radius or area). It is distinct from MI ratios and from radial asymmetry. FunMel’s matched assessment currently targets MI; other outcomes and inhibition models must be specified separately.

Warning/status Meaning and action
Fitted illumination range Pre-correction green-channel surface range, not residual error
flat_field_clipped_fraction Fraction of dish pixels where gains exceed correction limits; inspect calibration
residual_agar_range_pct Remaining spatial-bin median variation on fitted agar pixels; not validated colony-level error
segmentation_trim_fraction Narrow target/central connection removed; inspect the refined outline
Undetected colony No adequate region found; do not invent MI
not_resolved halo Uncertain boundary; do not call it biological zero
Pending coefficient Metadata/QC/missing-value issue; read its explicit reason
Inferential status other than ok Review model/replication; descriptive ratios may still be available

Flat-field fitting is not a substitute for comparable photography and exposure. Use diffuse, consistent lighting and an appropriate reference where possible. An agar reference is justified only for comparable, untinted medium; a reference card needs known colour and suitable placement. Unrecoverable clipping or organism colour gradients cannot be solved reliably by an image-only illumination model.

9. Continue with runnable examples 

source(system.file("examples","01_image_quickstart.R",package="FunMel"))
source(system.file("examples","02_coefficient_arithmetic.R",package="FunMel"))
source(system.file("examples","03_fungal_matched_experiment.R",package="FunMel"))

The bundled 14-day dataset is a worked case study. Its metadata has unverified folder-derived identities, and each set has three treatment plates and one control plate. That does not meet the built-in inference guard. Its technical review is bundled in validation/photo_review.zip; successful detection counts do not certify biological masks or calibration. None of its filenames are required by the generic image or coefficient functions.

The separate guides/FunMel_overview.md explains ImageJ complementarity, properties, functions and the algorithms. ImageJ/Fiji already offers ROI measurement and macro automation; no head-to-head superiority in accuracy or speed is claimed.
